text.title: event-sourcing-basics Failure Modes
text.summary: Failure modes observed when applying the event-sourcing-basics methodology. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix. Two critical event sourcing violations: mutable events, and oversized catch-all events.

antipattern.symptom: Engineer 'fixes a typo' in a stored event; replay diverges; audit trail compromised.
antipattern.fix: Make event tables append-only; add INSERT-only DB grant; correct via a Compensated event.

antipattern.symptom: Event named 'PlaceOrder'; downstream confuses command and fact.
antipattern.root-cause: Author named the trigger, not the result.

antipattern.symptom: Command handler sets order.status='placed' directly without emitting an event.
antipattern.fix: Route every state change through apply_new(OrderPlaced(...)).

antipattern.symptom: Two concurrent appends both succeed at version=4; replay diverges.
antipattern.fix: Add expected_version on append; reject if stream moved.

antipattern.symptom: Assigning new values to event fields after construction (e.g., event.customer_id = new_id).
antipattern.root-cause: Events stored in the event log become inconsistent with in-memory events. Replay produces different state than the original, making the event log unreliable as the source of truth.
antipattern.fix: Declare every event @dataclass(frozen=True) so assignment raises FrozenInstanceError; see the bad/good pair in 05-examples.xml.

antipattern.symptom: Mutable event: assigning to event.customer_id after construction.
antipattern.root-cause: Breaks immutability guarantee. Any code that cached the event has an inconsistent copy, making replay non-deterministic.
antipattern.fix: Same fix as fm-mutable-event-field-assignment (duplicate observation kept from 01-event-definitions): frozen=True on the Event base and every subclass.

antipattern.symptom: Using a single event type like OrderUpdated that carries the entire order state as a dict.
antipattern.root-cause: Loses intent (which field actually changed?), makes projections load unnecessary data, and makes schema evolution impossible without breaking all consumers that parse the dict.
antipattern.fix: Split into one event per change (OrderItemAdded, ShippingAddressChanged); see the bad/good pair in 05-examples.xml.

antipattern.symptom: Catch-all event: OrderUpdated with entire_order_data: dict containing all order fields.
antipattern.root-cause: Loses intent (what specifically changed?), bloats the event log, and makes schema evolution impossible without breaking all existing consumers.
antipattern.fix: Same fix as fm-large-catch-all-event (duplicate observation kept from 01-event-definitions): granular events carrying only the data that changed.
